content_units: For   24 coworkers split into 6 teams  , this format gives you   6 rounds x 8 questions = 48 questions total  , with a mix of easy, medium, and a few stretch questions across   movies, TV, music, games, and entertainment history (1990–2020)  .
-   Suggested timing:   10–12 minutes per round, plus 5 minutes scoring between rounds
-   Estimated total event length:   90–110 minutes including intro and tie-breakers
- Write one answer per question on team sheet
- Accept close spellings unless the exact spelling is the point
- Read each question twice for clarity
- For music/quote rounds, allow one repeat
Round 1: Big-Screen Hits of the 1990s and 2000s
1. In  Titanic , what is the name of Leonardo DiCaprio’s character?
2. Which 1993 dinosaur movie was directed by Steven Spielberg?
3. What color pill does Neo take in  The Matrix ?
4. In  Mean Girls , what day is jokingly celebrated as “Mean Girls Day”?
5. Which 2008 superhero film featured Heath Ledger as the Joker?
6. In the  Harry Potter  films, what house is Harry sorted into?
7. Which Pixar movie from 2003 features a clownfish searching for his son?
8. What is the fictional African country in  Black Panther ?
Round 2: TV Everyone Has Probably Heard Of
1. What coffee shop do the friends often meet in on  Friends ?
2. On  The Office  (US), what company does the Scranton branch work for?
3. Which animated family lives at 742 Evergreen Terrace?
4. What is the name of the fictional continent where much of  Game of Thrones  takes place?
5. In  Stranger Things , what is the alternate dimension called?
6. Who hosts the reality competition series  RuPaul’s Drag Race ?
7. Which sitcom features the characters Leslie Knope and Ron Swanson?
8. What phrase does Chris Harrison often use on  The Bachelor  before a key reveal?
Answer:   “This is the final rose tonight.”
1. Which artist sang “…Baby One More Time”?
2. Which singer is known as “The Material Girl”?
3. What duo released “Hey Ya!” under the name OutKast?
7. Which singer headlined the 2012 Super Bowl halftime show and performed “Vogue”?
Round 4: Video Games and Gaming Culture
1. What color is the most iconic version of Mario’s hat?
2. In  Pokémon , Pikachu is what type?
3. Which block-building game became one of the best-selling games of all time?
4. What handheld company made the Game Boy?
5. In  The Legend of Zelda  series, what is the name of the hero players usually control?
6. What game franchise features the phrase “Finish Him!”?
7. Which 2016 mobile game had people walking around catching virtual creatures?
8. In  Among Us , what is the hidden role trying to sabotage the crew?
1. What do the initials MTV stand for?
2. Which annual film awards are also called the Oscars?
3. What streaming service released  House of Cards  as its first major original hit drama?
4. Which social media/video platform, launched in 2005, became central to internet entertainment?
5. What long-running sketch comedy show premiered in 1975 and remained hugely influential through 1990–2020?
6. Which awards honor excellence in television in the United States?
7. What was the name of Apple’s digital music store launched in 2003?
8. Which 2020 streaming service launched with  The Mandalorian  as a flagship original?
Round 6: Mixed Pop Culture Grab Bag
1. What toy franchise features characters like Woody and Buzz Lightyear?
2. Who is the pop star behind the alter ego Sasha Fierce?
3. What is the name of the wizarding sport played on broomsticks in  Harry Potter ?
4. Which 2004 movie popularized the line, “I’m just one stomach flu away from my goal weight”?
If you want to avoid quote-specific sensitivity, swap this out with:
“Which magazine does Andy Sachs work for in  The Devil Wears Prada ?”
6. In the Marvel Cinematic Universe, what metal is Captain America’s shield primarily made from?
7. Which reality TV family helped make “Keeping Up with the Kardashians” a major hit?
8. What 1996 sci-fi film features the line “Welcome to Earth” and an alien invasion?
Use standard scoring for simplicity and pace.
Round   Questions   Points per Correct Answer   Round Max   Notes
-   Bonus option:   Add   1 bonus point   per round for the funniest team name or best mini-theme outfit, if you want a social twist
- If using bonus points, announce that clearly before starting
- Give each team one answer sheet per round
- Have teams swap papers with another team for quick scoring
- Host reads answers aloud after each round
- One organizer keeps a visible leaderboard after rounds 2, 4, and 6
Use these only if two or more teams are tied for a prize position.
- In what year did the first  Toy Story  movie release?
- Approximately how many seasons of  Friends  aired?
- What is the name of the kingdom in Disney’s  Frozen ?
- Ask alternating teams a broad pop-culture question until one misses
- Use   closest without going over   for number questions, or just   closest overall
- For sudden death, alternate which team answers first on each new question
- Keep tie-breakers easier than the hardest main-round questions
Host Notes for an Inclusive, Mixed-Knowledge Crowd
- Avoid overloading on one niche fandom
- Mix formats: blockbuster films, sitcoms, reality TV, chart music, family-friendly games, streaming culture
- Read all questions clearly and slowly
- Avoid trick wording unless it is very light
- Accept equivalent answers when the intent is correct
- Avoid obscure release dates unless used as tie-breakers
- Skip questions built around highly specific celebrity gossip
- Add a   music clip mini-round   by replacing 2 written music questions with 10-second audio clips
- Add a   picture question sheet   between rounds if you want a visual bonus round
- Let each team choose one   double-points question   before the event starts for extra excitement
This set is designed from widely known pop-culture material spanning film, TV, music, gaming, and entertainment trends from   roughly 1990–2020  , with mainstream emphasis for broad workplace play.
